# Part 1 — Read/Write Sets and Conflict Enumeration

## Read and Write Sets

| Txn | Read Set RS(Ti) | Write Set WS(Ti) |
|---|---|---|
| T1 | {A, B} | {A, B} |
| T2 | {A, B} | {A, B} |
| T3 | {A, B} | **∅** (read-only) |

Every pair of transactions conflicts on every item — T1/T2 mutually, and T1/T2 against T3 via their writes.

## Conflict List (operation-level, all pairs)

Using the schedule from the prior analysis: T1 and T2 both read `v0`; T1 commits first; T3 reads `v0`. Types: **rw** = anti-dependency (reads a version later overwritten), **wr** = reads-from, **ww** = version-order overwrite. Read–read pairs (T1.R / T2.R on A and B) are never conflicts and are omitted.

**Pair T1 ↔ T2** (both items shown; A and B behave identically):

| Item | Operation pair | Type | Direction | Outcome under SI |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | T2.R(A) vs T1.W(A) | **rw** | T1 → T2 | T2 read v0; T1 overwrote it |
| B | T2.R(B) vs T1.W(B) | **rw** | T1 → T2 | same |
| A | T1.R(A) vs T2.W(A) | **rw** | T2 → T1 | T1 read v0; T2's overwrite never materializes (aborted) |
| B | T1.R(B) vs T2.W(B) | **rw** | T2 → T1 | same |
| A | T1.W(A) vs T2.W(A) | **ww** | T1 → T2 | **FCW validation aborts T2** |
| B | T1.W(B) vs T2.W(B) | **ww** | T1 → T2 | FCW aborts T2 |
| A, B | T1.W → T2.R / T2.W → T1.R | **wr** | — | **None**: both read `v0` from T0, not from each other |

> The bidirectional rw pair is the signature of a lost-update candidate: each transaction reads the version the other overwrites.

**Pair T1 ↔ T3** and **Pair T2 ↔ T3** (T3 writes nothing → no ww, no outgoing conflicts):

| Item | Operation pair | Type | Direction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | T1.W(A) vs T3.R(A) | **rw** | T1 → T3 | T3 read v0, T1 wrote v1. If T3 instead snapshots v1, this becomes **wr** (T1 → T3) |
| B | T1.W(B) vs T3.R(B) | **rw** | T1 → T3 | same |
| A, B | T2.W vs T3.R | rw | T2 → T3 | **moot** — T2 aborted; excluded from the committed graph |

# Part 2 — Serialization Graph

## Nodes and Directed Edges — Committed MVSG (T2 aborted by FCW)

**Nodes:** `T0` (hypothetical initial writer of v0), `T1`, `T3`

```
T0 --wr(A,B)--> T1      T1 reads v0(A), v0(B)
T0 --wr(A,B)--> T3      T3 reads v0(A), v0(B)
T1 --rw(A,B)--> T3      T1 overwrites the v0 versions T3 read
```

**Acyclicity check:** Topological sort `T0 → T3 → T1` succeeds; no node has a path back to an ancestor.

**✅ ACYCLIC → the committed history {T1, T3} is conflict-preserving and view-serializable. Equivalent serial order: T0 → T3 → T1.**

(If T3's snapshot were taken after T1 commits, the `rw` edge becomes `wr(T1→T3)` and the order is T0 → T1 → T3 — still acyclic. T3's placement never creates a cycle because it is read-only.)

## Counterfactual Graph — if T2 were allowed to commit (no FCW)

```
T0 --wr--> T1, T2, T3
T1 --ww(A,B)--> T2        v1 → v2 version order
T1 --rw--> T2             T2 read v0; T1 overwrote
T2 --rw--> T1             T1 read v0; T2 overwrote   ← CYCLE
T1 --rw--> T3, T2 --rw--> T3
```

**Cycle: `T1 ⇄ T2` (the 2-cycle formed by the two mutual rw edges). ❌ CYCLIC → not serializable.**

## Serialization Result

| Graph | Cycles? | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Committed MVSG (T1, T3) | None | **Serializable** — order T0 → T3 → T1 |
| Unrestricted graph (T1, T2, T3 all commit) | T1 ⇄ T2 | **Not serializable** — lost-update cycle |

The ww conflict between T1 and T2 is exactly what snapshot isolation's first-committer-wins check detects at T2's commit; aborting T2 removes it and every edge touching it, leaving the acyclic committed graph above. The serialization result is therefore: **SI accepts the history, serializable, at the cost of aborting T2.**
